jobs.description: Career Category Research Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Senior Director, R&D Capability Enablement What you will do Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will translate R&D strategy into learning experiences, role readiness, and development opportunities that build workforce capability across R&D. In partnership with R&D leaders and functional learning partners, the role defines how priority capabilities are built, designs the experiences that enable them, and prepares employees to perform successfully. Working with R&D leaders and subject matter experts, the Senior Director translates business priorities into learning experiences and content that is accurate, useful, and easy to find. The role leads instructional designers, establishes content creation standards and a content management strategy, and uses learning analytics to show leaders what is working, where capability gaps remain, and where to focus investment. What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a person with these qualifications. Key Responsibilities Capability Strategy & Needs Partner with R&D leaders to identify current and emerging capability needs tied to scientific priorities, operating plans, and workforce plans. Use colleague feedback, capability assessments, performance data, and business priorities to identify gaps and sequence learning investments. Maintain a rolling capability roadmap and review it with R&D leadership at least twice a year. Learning Experience & Instructional Design Leadership Lead and develop instructional designers, set portfolio priorities, allocate work, and coach the team on learning design and delivery. Design role-based learning journeys and pathways, using a 70/20/10 approach where appropriate and drawing on instructor-led, digital, experiential, and coached learning. Create curricula and end-to-end learning experiences for priority capabilities, including instructional design, content development, and facilitation in partnership with subject matter experts. R&D Capability Architecture & Framework Translate leadership-defined R&D priorities into a shared capability architecture and framework, including core capabilities and proficiency expectations. Partner with leaders across R&D functions, including clinical development, data science, translational science, and research, to align priorities and provide guidance on competencies for critical roles. Translate the framework into role-based learning architecture, journeys, pathways, and manager resources that functions can use in their day-to-day work. Use feedback from learners and leaders, along with capability data, to update the framework as R&D needs change. Performance Readiness Oversee training governance, training management, and assignment processes for learning owned by Capability Enablement, with clear roles and standards. Develop end-to-end process learning for priority R&D workflows, partnering with process owners and functional teams on local learning needs. Define readiness expectations for priority functions and critical roles, and use appropriate checks to understand whether employees can perform required work. Advanced Capability Programs Design targeted programs for future-potential and high-potential R&D talent, including internships, rotations, mentorship, and focused development opportunities. Develop capability academies for priority R&D needs, such as AI application, when they address a defined business need. Focus these programs on targeted capability acceleration that complements Enterprise talent development and avoids duplicating existing programs. Learning Analytics & Business Impact Define measures for each learning goal, including reach, engagement, capability gains, application on the job, and relevant business outcomes. Create clear dashboards and reports so leaders can see participation, capability progress, persistent gaps, and trends across learning programs. Evaluate learning investments with appropriate assessments and business measures, explain the findings and their limits, and help leaders make informed prioritization and resourcing decisions. Content Standards & Management Strategy Set standards for learning content creation, including clear objectives, instructional design quality, accessibility, scientific accuracy, and subject matter review. Define a content management strategy for taxonomy, ownership, version control, discoverability, review cadence, archiving, and retirement. Maintain a curated R&D learning catalog and guide build, buy, reuse, and retirement decisions to reduce duplication and keep resources current. Operating Model & Functional Learning Partnership Design a learning operating model with clear governance, decision rights, service expectations, and ownership across central and functional teams. Partner with each R&D function to tailor enterprise capability builds to local needs through business consulting, prioritized capability builds, and critical-role consultation. Treat functional learning partnership as an operating approach, not a separate organization, and clarify ownership with R&D functions and Enterprise partners. Keep Capability Enablement focused on shared capability strategy, priority learning architecture and experiences, and common standards; functional teams retain ownership of local learning needs and process-specific education. Do not own function-specific competency models for every role, all process learning across R&D, Quality-owned GxP training, employee performance management, or programs that duplicate Enterprise offerings. Present capability and learning analytics to R&D leaders, connecting results to decisions about priorities and investment. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years in learning and development or a related field Strong expertise in adult learning, instructional design, performance consulting, and digital learning ecosystems. Experience designing and scaling enterprises or function-wide capability strategies Preferred Qualifications: 10 years in learning, capability, or organizational development, with significant time inside pharma/biotech R&D. Demonstrated experience designing, owning, or scaling a capability framework across multiple functions. Experience leading instructional designers or learning design teams and overseeing the quality of a broad learning portfolio. Experience designing role-based learning journeys, curricula, academies, or development programs for priority capabilities. Experience establishing learning content standards, governance, or a content management strategy. Experience using learning analytics and evaluation to guide decisions and communicate learning impact to leaders. At 2K, we create some of the most iconic and culture-shaping video games in entertainment, including NBA® 2K, one of the top-selling franchises in the world, and legendary titles like BioShock®, Borderlands®, Mafia, Sid Meier’s Civilization®, and XCOM®, as well as fan favorites WWE® 2K, TopSpin®, and PGA TOUR® 2K. We build unforgettable experiences by pushing the boundaries of creativity, authenticity and innovation across every genre.

Our portfolio is brought to life by some of the most influential game development studios in the world. Visual Concepts, Firaxis Games, Hangar 13, Cat Daddy Games, 31st Union, Cloud Chamber, Gearbox, HB Studios, and 2K SportsLab create world-class experiences across platforms.

But what truly powers 2K is our people.

We believe the best ideas come from teams that feel empowered, supported, and inspired. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive workplace where people are encouraged to come as they are and do their best work.

What We Need

The 2K SRE team owns the infrastructure behind every player connection — All 2K game services, account platforms, CI/CD pipelines, and developer tooling spanning AWS, GCP, and on-premises data centers across multiple global regions. Global launch windows and live-service events push systems to their limits, and this team is expected to hold the line.

Post-mortems here focus on systems, not people. Automation is the default answer to repetitive work. The infrastructure keeps millions of players connected — and the team takes that seriously!

The Senior SRE at 2K is a hands-on technical leader — shaping production infrastructure across multiple clouds and regions while partnering with network engineers, systems architects, and game studio developers. This is an ownership role: driving technical direction, influencing reliability from architecture review through production operation, and closing the gap between what engineering ships and what players experience.

What You'll Do

Platform & Infrastructure

Design, build, and operate scalable multi-cloud and hybrid infrastructure using Terraform, Pulumi, and GitOps workflows (ArgoCD, Flux). Own Kubernetes platforms (EKS, GKE) end-to-end — cluster lifecycle, multi-tenancy, networking (Istio, Cilium), and autoscaling — and push progressive delivery patterns (blue/green, canary) across game service deployments.

Observability & Reliability

•

Build and run the full observability stack: Prometheus + Grafana + Datadog

•

Define SLI/SLO/error budget policies and build alerting that cuts through the noise

•

Lead chaos engineering exercises to surface failure modes before players encounter them

•

Drive incident response and post-mortems with a focus on systemic fixes and real follow-through

Automation, Security & Developer Experience

Eliminate toil through self-service provisioning, automated remediation, and intelligent scaling. Harden CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, ArgoCD) . Embed security at the platform layer through secrets management (PasswordState, 1Password, and AWS Secrets Manager), policy-as-code (OPA/Gatekeeper).

Leadership

•

Promote SRE practices across 2K studios through reliability reviews, runbooks, and embedded collaboration

•

Shape architectural decisions and author engineering RFCs that move the platform forward

What Will Make You A Great Fit

Required Qualifications

•

5+ years in SRE, Platform Engineering, or equivalent infrastructure work at production scale

•

Deep Kubernetes experience in cloud environments (EKS or GKE preferred) — networking, storage, multi-cluster patterns

•

Strong IaC proficiency with Terraform and/or Pulumi; hands-on with Helm, Terragrunt, and GitOps tooling (ArgoCD or GitHub Actions)

•

Modern and Legacy Tech: AWS, GCP, VMware, and Bare metal servers

•

Server Configuration using Ansible, Puppet, and AWS Systems Manager

•

Observability stack experience: Datadog, Prometheus + Grafana, and OpenTelemetry,

•

SLI/SLO/error budget fluency — including how to operationalize them inside engineering teams

•

Production-quality code in Go, Python, or TypeScript: tools, automation, and internal libraries

•

Linux internals, TCP/IP networking, DNS, and TLS — proven enough to debug at the system level

•

Incident response and post-mortem leadership with a track record of systemic follow-through

Preferred Qualifications

•

Live-service game or large-scale consumer internet experience at millions of concurrent users

•

Service mesh depth (Istio, Cilium) and advanced Kubernetes networking

•

FinOps and managing resources at cloud scale

•

Experience with AI and Agentic Development

•

Cloud certifications (AWS Solutions Architect, GCP Professional Cloud Architect, CKA/CKS, or equivalent)

•

Experience mentoring SREs or leading reliability working groups

This role maintains relationships and favorable contacts with current accounts/patients and provides the ability to ensure patients have the required equipment to support their home healthcare needs.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Acts as a single point of contact for a specific account or accounts.
• Responds to customer needs, concerns and complaints in a timely manner.
• Consults with clients and referral sources on products and necessary equipment.

• Obtains all required documentation for orders to be entered into the system, service scheduling and billing/payment.
• Contacts patients to confirm orders and communicates any financial obligations before referral for delivery/service scheduling.

Hourly Pay - $26.19 -$38.47

OTHER DUTIES

• Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education and/or Experience

• High School diploma required

• At least 2 years of related experience
• Must be at least 21 years of age or older at the time of hire.

• Demonstrated ability to build and maintain solid working relationships with internal and external customers.

• Learn and comply with all Department of Transportation, Transportation Safety Management (TSM) and POV requirements applicable for the safe and complaint use of Apria vehicles and POVs.

• Participate in and successfully complete ongoing training and development to become and remain qualified to perform the essential job functions.

• Geographically located within the assigned territory.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations or Professional Designations

• Must Poses a Valid Driver’s License

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES

• Business Acumen
• Problem Solving/Analysis
• Communication Proficiency
• Personal Effectiveness/Credibility

Computer Skills

• Basic skills in Access, Excel, PowerPoint, MS Project, Visio, Word

Language Skills

• English (reading, writing, verbal)

Mathematical Skills

• Basic level mathematical proficiency, with a strong ability to understand, interpret and develop spreadsheet data

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this job, the employee uses his/her hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, or crouch; talk or hear. The employee uses computer and telephone equipment. Specific vision requirements of this job include close vision and distance vision. Must be able to travel by plane and automobile (if applicable). In addition:

• Regularly required to use hands to write, use computer, operate a motor vehicle, use a hand-held device, telephone and use a document imaging system and manipulate documents.

• Regularly required to read documents and write neatly, legibility and transcribe accurate information and numbers/values.

• Employee continually engages in activities that require talking and hearing.

• This position requires frequent variations including sitting, walking, standing, kneeling, reaching or stooping.

• The employee must be able to safely operate and possess and maintain a valid driver’s license, specific to vehicle operated in the conduct of this job.

• Specific vision abilities required to perform this job safely include close vision, distant vision, night (low to limited light) vision and the ability to adjust focus to work on a computer and read documents.

The physical demands and work environment characteristics described above are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

While performing the duties of this job, the employee rarely is exposed to fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals. The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate. In addition:

• General lighting is generally provided via florescent lighting indoors, and natural lighting outdoors, and low light conditions consistent with outdoor and/or night working environment.

• May be required to receive vaccinations and participate in medical assessments and testing consistent with the work environment or patients exposed to.

• Will be required to wear various personal protective equipment consistent with the hazards encountered in this role.

This role leads supplier relationship management initiatives and collaborates with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Capital Projects, Environmental, and Functional stakeholders to deliver procurement and value creation strategies.

The Category Manager is responsible for sourcing, supplier management, contract negotiations, and commercial support for a diverse portfolio of service categories including maintenance, construction, environmental services, specialized crafts, and project-related services. The position identifies and drives continuous improvement opportunities, oversees contract implementation and supplier performance, and serves as a strategic business partner supporting both day-to-day manufacturing operations and capital investment initiatives.

This position can be located in either Pasadena, Texas or in Irving, Texas.

Responsibilities:

• Develop and implement category strategies for Industrial and Technical Services across the Americas region.
• Lead strategic sourcing initiatives, competitive bidding events, and supplier negotiations for maintenance, construction, environmental, and project-related services.
• Build strong partnerships with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, EHS, and Capital Project stakeholders to understand business requirements and develop procurement solutions.
• Negotiate and administer complex service agreements, master service agreements, project contracts, and related commercial terms and conditions.
• Lead supplier relationship management activities including performance reviews, scorecards, business reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.
• Drive value creation through cost optimization, process improvements, supplier innovation, and risk mitigation.
• Support capital projects by providing sourcing strategy, commercial negotiation, contract development, and supplier management expertise.
• Ensure suppliers meet safety, compliance, sustainability, and operational performance expectations.
• Identify opportunities to standardize services, leverage spend, and improve total cost of ownership across manufacturing sites.
• Resolve commercial and supplier performance issues while maintaining productive business relationships.
• Utilize procurement systems, sourcing tools, market intelligence, and data analytics to support decision-making and category management activities.
• Collaborate with Procurement leadership and category peers to support broader procurement initiatives and organizational objectives.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Procurement, Business, Engineering, Construction Management, or related discipline; equivalent experience may be considered.
• 7–15 years of professional experience in Procurement, Supply Chain, Engineering, Construction Management, Operations, Maintenance, or related industrial fields.
• Demonstrated experience negotiating contracts and managing supplier relationships.
• Experience supporting manufacturing, industrial, chemical, energy, or heavy industrial operations preferred.
• Experience supporting capital projects, construction projects, maintenance programs, or engineering services strongly preferred.
• Strong understanding of legal, commercial, and risk management concepts within service agreements.
• Project management experience preferred.
• CPSM, CPSD, PMP, C.P.M., or similar professional certification preferred.

Preferred Category Experience

• Maintenance Services
• Mechanical, Electrical, and Instrumentation Services
• Environmental Services
• Waste Management
• Specialized Craft Services
• Industrial Construction
• Turnaround and Outage Services
• Engineering Services
• Capital Project Support Services
• Industrial Facility Services
• Technical Consulting Services

Skills, Knowledge & Abilities

• Strategic sourcing and category management expertise.
• Strong commercial and contract negotiation skills.
• Ability to influence stakeholders across multiple functions and organizational levels.
• Excellent communication and relationship management capabilities.
• Strong analytical and data-driven decision-making skills.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities across geographically dispersed manufacturing locations.
• Demonstrated problem-solving and continuous improvement mindset.
• Strong financial acumen and understanding of total cost of ownership concepts.
• High ethical standards and commitment to safety, compliance, and responsible sourcing.

Key Personal Qualities

• Strategic thinker who can balance long-term value creation with day-to-day business support.
• Self-starter who thrives in a dynamic manufacturing environment.
• Strong collaborator capable of building credibility with technical and operational stakeholders.
• Results-oriented with a bias for action and accountability.

• Naturally curious and willing to learn new categories and business processes.

jobs.description: At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus. We own the full stack, from silicon through the software that makes it work (compilers, runtimes, drivers, and the frameworks that let customers run workloads on our hardware). Annapurna has ASIC teams across a range of products and disciplines, and we work to place you on a technical team aligned with your interests and strengths. Example teams and focus areas include: - RTL design for machine learning accelerators (Trainium/Inferentia) - Design verification and functional validation - Physical design, timing closure, and place-and-route - SoC integration and chip architecture Throughout the interview process, we will partner with you and our hiring managers to match you to a team where your background and interests fit best, so your project is something you're genuinely excited to work on. As an ASIC Engineer Intern, you'll contribute to real chip development work, which may include: - Designing and implementing RTL for digital logic blocks using Verilog/SystemVerilog - Developing and running verification environments to validate design functionality and coverage - Supporting synthesis, timing analysis, and physical design flows - Debugging design issues through simulation and analysis - Collaborating with architecture, verification, and physical design teams to take features from specification to silicon - Documenting your design decisions and presenting your work to the team You'll be paired with a mentor and manager who will help scope your project, support your growth, and set you up to deliver meaningful, measurable impact by the end of your internship.

jobs.description:
As Publishing Product Director, you are the creative custodian of one of Crytek’s games, embedded inside the game team, accountable for protecting the creative vision and translating the promise of the game into work that the publishing team can execute with conviction. The success of a great game depends on the work that surrounds it landing as truthfully as the game itself, and closing that gap is what this role exists to do. You make sure that what reaches players is authentic, aspirational, tells the story the game deserves, and delights the players who play it.

The game in your remit is an unannounced project in the Crytek portfolio. The work focuses on shaping the project’s player promise from the inside out, defining the publishing narrative for its eventual reveal, and carrying its creative vision through to launch and into ongoing releases.

You sit inside the game team, working shoulder-to-shoulder with game leadership every day. You partner directly with the Chief Publishing Officer and Brand & Marketing Director to support both the game and the business as one connected effort. You are the direct line between the game team and the publishing organization, the person who protects the north star on both ends, and the person both sides trust to tell them the truth.

This role demands creative conviction, drive, and the kind of experience that only comes from working shoulder-to-shoulder with game teams. You will protect the team from noise so they can build the game, and you will give the publishing team the clarity, player insight, and creative truth they need to land it well. It is one of the most consequential seats at Crytek, and one of the most rewarding.

• Be the custodian of the game’s creative vision, tone, and player promise, and translate it into work that publishing can execute with conviction • Sit embedded inside the game team and act as the daily bridge between game leadership and the publishing organisation • Serve as the source of truth on what the game is, what is coming next, and what it means for players, across Marketing, Comms, Community, and Commercial • Brief and review every major marketing, comms, and community output for creative authenticity, ensuring it tells the right player story • Partner with the Chief Publishing Officer and Brand & Marketing Director to shape go-to-market plans that serve the game and the business in equal measure • Drive franchise narrative, player promise, and creative direction across reveals, beats, and post-launch moments • Protect the game team from operational noise so they can focus on building, while translating publishing priorities into work the team can act on • Keep the north star intact on both ends, keeping publishing grounded in the game’s vision, and the game team grounded in player and market reality • 8+ years working at the seam between game development and publishing or marketing, with significant time embedded inside game teams • Proven ability to translate creative vision into commercial activation without compromising either side, with strong creative judgement and editorial instinct you can defend under pressure • Fluency across business models (premium, live service, DLC, F2P) and multi-year roadmap strategy, and how the two shape the player promise • Cross-functional leadership and the ability to influence without authority across game and publishing teams • Strong player insight, audience segmentation, and community fluency • Drive and operating range, comfortable moving from creative critique in the morning to commercial trade-offs in the afternoon • Experience supporting or launching at least one major game or live-service title from inside the game team • Track record of being trusted by both game leadership and publishing leadership
